title: Molina leads home Wittmann as Mortara climbs to third
dek: Miguel Molina won Race 1 at Hockenheim for Audi by 1.661 seconds from Marco Wittmann, while Edoardo Mortara fought from eighth to third to keep the title fight alive at 17 points.

chapters.title: Two races and 50 points still in play
text: The 2016 DTM season ended at the Hockenheimring with two races in two days, and when the cars rolled out on Saturday 15 October the drivers' title was still undecided. Marco Wittmann led the standings for BMW on 176 points, 14 clear of Audi's Edoardo Mortara, who had won the opening race of the previous round in Hungary. Jamie Green, third for Audi on 137, was still in theory in the hunt, while the best-placed Mercedes driver, Robert Wickens, was on 122 and could no longer reach Wittmann's total even with every point on offer.

The arithmetic gave Wittmann a route to an early celebration. With 25 points for a win, he would be champion on Saturday if he could stretch his lead to 26 or more, which meant gaining 12 points on Mortara in the race. Mortara, for his part, needed to take the fight to Sunday. The weekend was also a farewell: António Félix da Costa was contesting his final races in the DTM, driving the Schnitzer BMW.

Saturday's race was the 17th of the season's 18 races, with just one more to follow on Sunday. Wittmann, the 2014 champion, was chasing a second title, while Mortara had to keep him from sealing it on Saturday and then outscore him in the finale. Mercedes was out of the title fight, so the focus lay on Audi and BMW.

chapters.title: Da Costa takes pole, Wittmann fourth, Mortara eighth
text: Wittmann led qualifying at half distance, having moved to the top with a 1:32.526 after two session-best sectors and leading an Audi 2-3-4-5 when the drivers came in for their second runs. Then the order changed. Miguel Molina, running off-sequence on a largely empty track, took provisional pole with a 1:32.444 with about four minutes left, and da Costa answered almost at once with a 1:32.344, which stood to the end.

Da Costa's pole was 0.100 seconds clear of Molina, with Tom Blomqvist third on 1:32.508 in the RBM BMW. Wittmann improved only marginally on his second run and was demoted to fourth, 0.004 seconds behind fellow BMW driver Blomqvist and 0.168 off the pole time. Maxime Martin made it a BMW 1-3-4-5 on the grid with fifth place, Mike Rockenfeller was sixth in his Audi, and Augusto Farfus took seventh.

Mortara found a late improvement that lifted him from 15th to eighth, 0.318 seconds off the time of da Costa, with Timo Glock and Nico Müller completing the top ten. Green was only 14th, a result that left his outside chance of the title all but gone. Mercedes struggled across the board: Paul di Resta, 12th and less than half a second off pole, was the leading car of the eight Mercedes-AMGs.

chapters.title: Molina dives inside the pole-sitter
text: Molina, starting second, dived on the inside of da Costa into Turn 1 and took the lead on the opening lap. Wittmann held fourth through the first corners and moved up to third at the hairpin, then went ahead of da Costa into second place. Da Costa tried to put pressure on Molina in the opening stint, but Wittmann was soon ahead of him, and Molina began to draw clear.

Mortara's afternoon began with a setback. He gained a place early on but was shoved back to eighth by Glock at the Sachs Kurve, with the two touching on corner exit. Over the next laps he tried to use his DRS against the BMW without success. Felix Rosenqvist's Mercedes stopped after nine laps, the first car to leave the race. By then Wittmann was running about three seconds behind Molina, and a championship celebration on Saturday looked possible.

chapters.title: Four laps that kept the title alive
text: The turning point came in the middle of the race. Mortara finally went past Glock for seventh around lap 15, diving down the inside after the BMW had looked at a move on Farfus and backed out, then took Farfus on the lap after. By lap 18 he had also dealt with his Audi team-mate Mike Rockenfeller, who was busy with Blomqvist, and with the BMW driver himself, and was fourth.

Rockenfeller followed him past Blomqvist, and René Rast, in his Phoenix Audi, was soon through on the BMW as well, so that Blomqvist dropped back to the edge of the points. Mortara had by now put himself in range of da Costa, with only the closing laps left.

chapters.title: Molina clear, Mortara takes the last podium place
text: Molina drove to the flag in 43:02.346, his second win of the season and the third of his DTM career, leading from the first corner. Wittmann finished second, 1.661 seconds behind. Mortara closed on da Costa with about three minutes remaining, stayed in his slipstream, and made the decisive move at the hairpin with roughly a minute left, taking third. He could not get within DRS range of Wittmann and finished 1.144 seconds behind him.

Da Costa was fourth, 4.870 seconds behind the winner, with Rockenfeller fifth and Rast sixth for his first points in the series. Glock was seventh, Green eighth after climbing from 14th on the grid, Blomqvist ninth and di Resta tenth, collecting the one point Mercedes scored. Di Resta said he had been forced to use his DRS early and had none left to defend against Green, who still had his.
The result left Wittmann on 194 points and Mortara on 177, with the 17-point gap meaning that Wittmann needed only fifth place on Sunday to take the title. Green, on 141, was out of the fight.

facts.t: Molina wins from the first corner
facts.v: Miguel Molina passed pole-sitter António Félix da Costa into Turn 1 and led home Marco Wittmann by 1.661 seconds in 43:02.346.
